PUBLIC RESPONSE: Agency Law

The modern Israeli legal system began incorporating explicit "good faith" language only after the mid-1960s wave of civil-law codification statutes. Among those enactments the Agency Law (1965) contains the earliest statutory appearance of the phrase, predating the Sales Law (1968), the Pledges Law (1967), the Contracts (General Part) Law (1973) and all later remedial and specific-contract statutes. Later codes simply repeated and expanded the same formula; therefore the Agency Law is the first statute that introduced the concept.

Hence the Sale Law is the first modern Israeli statute to use the term.
